purpose: Classical Arabic grammar and lexicon reference works requested for future use in this project -- like references/tafsir, not read by the shipped app today.
notes: Unlike the tafsir works (see references/tafsir/manifest.json), none of these were found in a cleanly structured, directly downloadable form (a simple per-surah/per-entry JSON API) at any source reachable from this environment. Two leads were identified but not resolved to exact download paths within a reasonable research budget this session -- see each entry's `note`.

This sandbox's network policy blocks most non-GitHub domains outright (kitab-project.org, archive.org, shamela.ws, and others all returned connection-blocked errors), which ruled out several otherwise-promising leads before their content could even be checked.

requested.author: Sibawayh (d. 180 AH)
requested.note: Has a known identifier (0180Sibawayh.KitabSibawayh) in the OpenITI corpus (github.com/OpenITI), a large multi-repo collection of classical Arabic/Islamicate texts split into ~25-lunar-year-period repositories (e.g. OpenITI/0225AH). Locating the exact repo and file path requires either a metadata index file this session couldn't locate, or manually paging through OpenITI's repository list -- not completed here. kitab-project.org (the corpus's own browse/download UI) is blocked by this environment's network policy.

requested.author: Ibn Manzur (d. 711 AH)
requested.note: Bundled (alongside al-Qamus al-Muhit and several other classical lexicons) inside a compressed SQLite database in the wizsk/arabic_lexicons GitHub repo, built for an offline dictionary reader app. The database is distributed only via GitHub Releases (app build assets), not as a plain file in the repository tree, so it isn't fetchable via raw.githubusercontent.com the way this project's other data sources are -- and its license/redistribution terms for the underlying dictionary text weren't confirmed. Not pursued further this session.
